investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and both sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T15:00:04Z because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe never received a successful agent creation response, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected and all contract assertions went unverified. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real API-level rejection; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.
investigation.rootCause: The production Swarm API is rejecting new remote agent creation requests with a 409 Conflict because the eval's org has reached the hard agent quota limit of 100. Every attempt by the eval runner to call POST /api/agents — for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime — hits this quota wall before any agent is provisioned, preventing the probe from collecting any evidence and causing all three checks to fail with the identical error message. The quota exhaustion is the earliest violated contract boundary; the eval infrastructure itself is functioning correctly (the request was made and a structured error was returned within 1437 ms, well under the 120 000 ms outage threshold).

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured, consistent with the probe aborting immediately on the 409 before any agent lifecycle data could be recorded.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, confirming the probe never progressed past the creation call.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical 409 message, sameMessage=true — the runtime check also calls POST /api/agents and hit the same quota wall.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1331-1339: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1339 immediately after requireOrgId — the first API call in the probe is agent creation, so a quota rejection terminates the entire probe.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1437 — the 409 was returned almost instantly, consistent with a quota guard rejecting the request before any VM provisioning work began.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] The eval org's remote agent count has reached the Swarm API hard limit of 100. Prior eval runs or other activity created agents that were not cleaned up (e.g., withCleanup failed or was skipped), causing quota to accumulate until new creation is blocked.

[Medium confidence] A previous eval run's cleanup step (withCleanup) failed silently or was interrupted, leaving orphaned remote agents counted against the quota. The runner source at run-status-probes.mjs:1337 wraps creation in withCleanup, but if cleanup did not execute the agents persist.

[Lower confidence] The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered on the Swarm API side (a server-side configuration change), causing previously-passing runs to now exceed the limit even with normal cleanup behavior.

[Low confidence — hypothesis only, not supported by eval proof] Commit 7c8e040 (suspect-change.7c8e040) touched CI workflow files including .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml; it is possible a workflow change caused the eval to run more frequently or with a different org credential, accelerating quota consumption. However, 7c8e040's candidateTouchedPaths is empty and matchedNeedles is empty, so this remains unproven speculation.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Fails in production-api: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on Agent Runtime Endpoint
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=2064) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 response, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint is unreachable or misconfigured in that environment. The identical check passes in the desktop-release environment (latencyMs=147230, imageUrlPresent=true, generation_completed frame present), confirming the image generation pipeline itself is functional and the failure is isolated to the production-api harness connectivity layer.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api runtime environment cannot reach the agent runtime harness endpoint required to open a session for image generation. The stream emits a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and the message "agent runtime endpoint not found (404)", causing the stream to terminate before any generation_progress or generation_completed frames are emitted and before an image URL is produced. This is an eval-infrastructure or deployment-configuration failure scoped to the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so no claim of a user-facing production outage is made.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2064, far below the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, confirming the stream failed immediately rather than timing out.

sibling.image-generation-stream: desktop-release environment passed the same check (status=pass, imageUrlPresent=true, generation_completed present, latencyMs=147230), proving the image generation pipeline is functional and the failure is environment-specific.
expected-output.contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 267-273): contract requires frameTypes to contain 'generation_completed' and imageUrlPresent=true; both assertions failed.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1431-1439: runner calls apiSse against /api/generate/image/stream; the 404 is returned by the server-side routing layer before any generation work begins.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:237-245: production-api check is registered as required=false, statusImpact=informational, confirming this failure does not constitute a declared service outage by registry policy.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY: The agent runtime harness is not deployed or not reachable at the URL configured by LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL for the production-api environment. The 404 is returned before the session can be opened, blocking all downstream generation frames.

SECONDARY: The production-api environment is pointing to a harness deployment that is running an incompatible version (API contract mismatch), causing the endpoint route to return 404 even though the process is running.

TERTIARY: The LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL environment variable is absent, empty, or set to a stale/incorrect value in the CI or runtime context that executed this eval, causing the request to resolve to a non-existent endpoint.

LOW-CONFIDENCE HYPOTHESIS: Commit 7c8e040 (suspect-change.7c8e040, committedAt=2026-06-16T14:54:10Z, ~6 minutes before the eval ran at 15:00:07Z) touched .github/actions/setup-harness-sibling/action.yml and .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml among other CI files. If this commit altered harness setup steps or environment variable injection for the production-api workflow, it could have broken harness reachability. This remains a hypothesis only; the commit's candidateTouchedPaths list is empty and no source diff is available to confirm causality.
